name: Reel-Edit
tagline: OpenReel Video — a professional video editor for HarmonyOS 2in1
upstreamNote: OpenReel Video by Augani and contributors · 5.2k★ · MIT. The editor is upstream's work, used unmodified apart from three platform changes.
description: A port of OpenReel Video — a browser-based, no-cloud, no-watermark video editor — to HarmonyOS PC. The upstream editor (timeline, engine, Media/Text/Graphics/Effects panels, Viewer, Inspector, export pipeline) runs unmodified inside an ArkWeb host. What this repo adds is the HarmonyOS half: an ArkTS module, a native H.264/AAC + MP4 muxer over the platform media framework, a JS bridge, and the build and release tooling.
features: The full editor: start screen, project formats, panels, Viewer, Inspector, Timeline, undo/redo, clip selection
Project create and open, persisting across launches
Export end to end: DocumentViewPicker save dialog, renderer frame stream, native MP4 muxer with video + audio tracks
Light and dark themes that follow the device setting
863 upstream tests green; the web bundle is typechecked on every build
porting: Pattern: native web host — ArkWeb serves the upstream bundle over a virtual https://openreel.harmony.local origin, because ArkWeb blocks cross-origin sub-resource loads from file:// and resource://

Bridge: window.openreel reimplemented in ArkTS and registered with registerJavaScriptProxy — registered *synchronous*, because the async proxy does not marshal a returned Promise; replies arrive via window.__openreelResolve(id, payload)
Binary payloads cross the JSON proxy as base64, and export frames travel the same way — createWebMessagePorts + postMessage succeeds natively but never reaches the page

Native export: reel_export.c replaces the FFmpeg sidecar with OH_VideoEncoder (H.264) + OH_AudioEncoder (AAC) + OH_AVMuxer (MP4), reproducing its frame-credit backpressure so the renderer throttling loop is unchanged

Platform traps documented in the README: the API 24 buffer interface is index-based, and OH_AVCODEC_MIMETYPE_* are exported as functions rather than data — reading them through the pointer yields a code address and every call fails with AV_ERR_INVALID_VAL

Three upstream changes: no in-app window controls (HarmonyOS draws its own), theme blocks inside explicit prefers-color-scheme so the device wins, and OPENREEL_HARMONY=1 removing the WebCodecs export path that would bypass the native encoder
install:
pnpm install
pnpm --filter @openreel/core build:wasm   # engine WASM, not checked in
./scripts/build-harmony.sh              # typecheck + web bundle + HAP
hdc install -r entry/build/default/outputs/default/entry-default-unsigned.hap
disclaimer: Upstream OpenReel Video © Augani and contributors, MIT — all credit for the editor belongs to them. Debug builds are unsigned; a signed HAP needs a certificate, key and provisioning profile bound to com.reeledit.harmony that only Huawei issues. The 2in1 emulator image ships with no H.264 or AAC encoder, so MP4 export stops there and the app says so; on hardware the same pipeline is expected to finish. Desktop only — upstream blocks viewports under 768px.

name: OpenGMaps SDK
tagline: Google Maps SDK for OpenHarmony & HarmonyOS
description: Google Maps as a reusable SDK for the HarmonyOS ecosystem. A Flutter backport by HarmoniProductions that wraps Google Maps (GMaps) for OpenHarmony & HarmonyOS — no GMS binary ships on OHOS, so it carries an in-house platform interface over the Maps JS API in ArkWeb, plus Places / Geocoding / Directions clients and native Location Kit.
features: Google Maps vector tiles, 4 map types, markers and routes via stock GoogleMap API
Debounced Places Autocomplete + text search + POI-tap place cards
Driving / walking / cycling / transit routes with polyline + steps
Saved places + recents in OHOS preferences, my-location dot
Honest no-key state — never renders a fake map
porting: Pattern: Flutter backport shim — platform interface → JSON → JS bridge
Dart-only backport: camera, overlays, events + poiTaps extension
Native channels only for location + storage (io.opengmaps/…)
Permissions: INTERNET + LOCATION / APPROXIMATELY_LOCATION
install:
fvm flutter run -d <ohos-device> --dart-define=GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY=KEY
# or: fvm flutter build hap --debug … && hdc install …hap
disclaimer: GMaps data © Google. Key use subject to Google terms + billing. By HarmoniProductions.

name: OpenTwit
tagline: Open X client for HarmonyOS devices
description: Open-source X client built native in ArkTS: a Stage-model app with Home timeline, Explore, Alerts, DMs and Me tabs. Signs in with X via OAuth 2.0 PKCE in an embedded browser; shows sample posts with zero setup and reports paid-access (402) states honestly. Phone, tablet and 2in1 from one HAP.
features: Home timeline with reply / repost / like / views, pull-to-refresh
Floating compose button with bottom-sheet editor (replies prefill @handle)
Sign in with X via OAuth 2.0 PKCE — the only auth, no keys to handle
Explore + search, Alerts, DMs, Me tab with profile card and sign-out
Zero-setup sample posts; honest 402 paid-access status messages
porting: Pattern: native ArkTS Stage client over the X API — no shim, no server
Auth seam: OAuth 2.0 PKCE in an embedded browser, token in preferences
UI seam: Navigation + bottom Tabs, HarmonyOS SymbolGlyph icons
One HAP for phone / tablet / 2in1 (EntryAbility, responsive layout)
install:
hvigorw assembleHap --mode module -p product=default
hdc install entry/build/default/outputs/default/entry-default-unsigned.hap
disclaimer: Unofficial X client. X and Twitter are trademarks of X Corp. Free-tier API limits (HTTP 402) apply — expect restricted actions without paid access.

name: OpenTwit Web
tagline: The real x.com web app inside a native HarmonyOS shell
description: x.com itself, running in the system Web component — and every piece of chrome rebuilt as native HarmonyOS. Per-tab headers with a Home "For you / Following" switcher that drives the page's real timeline tab, Explore's search field in the header, the account menu, the compose FAB and sheet, and a bottom bar that turns into a side rail past 840 vp. X's own navigation and floating buttons are stripped by injected CSS/JS, so the shell never double-renders chrome.
features: Full web Twitter — /home, /explore, /notifications, /messages, profile, settings — signed in with web cookies, no API key
Native headers per tab: avatar + timeline switcher on Home, live search on Explore, title over subtitle elsewhere, one gear at most
Bottom bar with filled HarmonyOS Symbols becomes a side rail past 840 vp — phone, tablet, unfolded foldable and 2in1 from one HAP
Native account menu, compose FAB and bottom sheet that posts through x.com's own submit and reports a native toast
X's top nav, bottom nav and page headers removed by injected CSS/JS; the shell reads document.title and aria-selected back to stay in step
Route-aware user agent, offline retry card, render-process recovery, haptic tick on tab change
Layered app icon, system colour resources for real light/dark, app.string localisation (en + zh_CN) — guideline audit in the repo
porting: Pattern: native web shell — system Web component + native ArkUI chrome; no shim, no companion server
Seam: common/WebConfig.ets holds the route table, per-route user agent and URL→tab mapping
Seam: common/WebChrome.ets injects CSS/JS that strips X's own chrome and reads page state back
Web hardening: DOM storage on, mixed mode compatible, file access off, WebDarkMode.Auto, custom UA OpenTwit-Web/1.0 HarmonyOS
Build: ohpm install → hvigorw assembleHap → scripts/sign-hap.sh → hdc install
install:
ohpm install && hvigorw assembleHap --no-daemon
./scripts/sign-hap.sh
hdc uninstall com.opentwit.web   # a bundle cannot switch signing identities
hdc install dist/OpenTwit-Web-1.0.0-signed.hap
disclaimer: Unofficial web shell for x.com. X and Twitter are trademarks of X Corp. Your session lives in the system Web component's cookie store. The signed HAP carries the OpenHarmony test identity — retail devices need an AppGallery certificate and profile for com.opentwit.web.

name: OHEmacs
description: Emacs ported to OHOS: Stage-model HAP with XComponent surface + NAPI libentry.so + EGL rendering. Stage 1 GUI shell launches and renders (Harmony_PC_61 verified); Stage 2 brings the full Lisp engine via an ohos display backend + two-stage pdump cross-compile.
features: Stage-model HAP, XComponent surface, EGL render loop
NAPI event queue (touch + resize verified via hilog)
ohos display backend scaffold (ohosterm / ohosfns / ohosfont)
Documented cross-compile + on-device emacs.pdmp plan
porting: Pattern: native ArkTS shell + NAPI bridge to the C upstream
Upstream GNU Emacs 30.1, approach cloned from the Android port
Build: ohpm install → hvigorw assembleHap → hdc install
See docs/PORTING.md + CROSS_PROBE.md in the repo
install:
ohpm install
hvigorw assembleHap --mode module -p product=default
hdc install entry/build/default/outputs/default/entry-default-unsigned.hap
disclaimer: GNU Emacs © Free Software Foundation. OHOS shell is Apache-2.0.

name: WhatIsIt
description: Native ArkUI WhatsApp client whose session lives on a Go whatisit-server (whatsmeow + meowcaller, SQLite, keepalive). Link once via in-app QR or 8-char phone code; the server keeps the Multi-Device session alive. Chats over HTTP + WebSocket push, media cached server-side.
features: QR + phone-code pairing, SHORTCAKE passkey flow (dev fallback)
1:1 + group text, replies, reactions, ticks, read receipts
Media send/receive, full-history sync, on-demand backfill
Status + Channels tabs; session survives server restarts
WhatsApp-native voice/video via meowcaller (not yet device-validated)
porting: Pattern: companion-server bridge — ArkTS app ⇄ Go server ⇄ WA protocol
server-go is current (wire-compatible with the Rust server/ reference)
App seam: CdpBridge.ets + PasskeyService + CallService / XComponent
Deploy: Go 1.25+ anywhere, VPS + Caddy / Cloudflare Tunnel for TLS
install:
cd server-go && go run ./cmd/server  # :18770
# app: oniro-app build && oniro-app app apply && oniro-app app launch
disclaimer: Unofficial client — may violate Meta ToS (ban risk). One account per server IP. No browser / Chrome / Jitsi path.
